samples.summary: TextEditor.toggleList's new heading-restoring exit has no test at all
samples.evidence: The diff changes three toggleList implementations and the new test file only exercises one of them (`initialize`/EditorAPI in packages/docs/test/view/list-heading-roundtrip.test.ts:192-249). `TextEditor.toggleList` (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:2164-2172) is private and only reachable via the Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+7 / +8 shortcuts (text-editor.ts:957-968); I found no test that dispatches those keys or otherwise reaches it. The stated purpose of `unlistedBlockType` is to keep these three implementations from drifting, yet two of the three call sites can regress (e.g. reverting to hardcoded 'paragraph') with the suite still green.
searchedFor: read text-editor.ts keyboard handler around lines 950-970

samples.summary: Docs text-box editor toggleList exit only covered by a smoke test that asserts nothing about the behavior
samples.evidence: The only existing coverage of this API is packages/docs/test/view/text-box-editor.test.ts:327-333, which asserts `typeof api.toggleList === 'function'` and `expect(() => api.toggleList('unordered')).not.toThrow()` — those pass identically whether the exit type is a restored heading or a hardcoded paragraph. No test bullets a heading in a text box and un-bullets it to assert `type === 'heading'` / `headingLevel`.

samples.summary: The new invariant that a retained headingLevel is 'inert' on a list-item is asserted nowhere
samples.evidence: The `Block` doc comment added at packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:54-61 claims every reader (export, `blockStyleId`, toolbar labels) gates on `type === 'heading'`, and this is the load-bearing safety argument for keeping `headingLevel` on list items. No test in the diff pins that: no assertion that `blockStyleId({type:'list-item',headingLevel:2})==='normal'`, that markdown/docx/pdf export of a bulleted heading emits a list item rather than a heading, or that `getBlockLabel('list-item', 2)` (packages/frontend/src/components/text-formatting/text-style-options.ts:112) still says 'Normal text'. The code currently gates correctly, so a future reader that switches to `headingLevel !== undefined` would break silently.
searchedFor: Grep 'headingLevel' in packages/docs/test (no inertness assertions found)

samples.summary: No test that the heading's block style/spacing survives the bullet round trip
samples.evidence: `setBlockType` re-materializes `block.style` whenever `blockStyleId` changes (packages/docs/src/store/memory.ts:272-274), so heading→list-item→heading materializes 'normal' spacing and then heading spacing again. The new tests only assert `type` and `headingLevel` (list-heading-roundtrip.test.ts:209-249); nothing asserts what happens to user-set spacing/margins across the round trip, which is the other user-visible half of 'gives the heading back'.
searchedFor: read the whole new test file for style/margin assertions

finding.summary: TextEditor.toggleList's new heading-restoring exit has no test at all
finding.evidence: The diff changes three toggleList implementations and the new test file only exercises one of them (`initialize`/EditorAPI in packages/docs/test/view/list-heading-roundtrip.test.ts:192-249). `TextEditor.toggleList` (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:2164-2172) is private and only reachable via the Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+7 / +8 shortcuts (text-editor.ts:957-968); I found no test that dispatches those keys or otherwise reaches it. The stated purpose of `unlistedBlockType` is to keep these three implementations from drifting, yet two of the three call sites can regress (e.g. reverting to hardcoded 'paragraph') with the suite still green.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. TextEditor.toggleList (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:2164-2180) uses the new unlistedBlockType exit and is private, reachable only from the '7'/'8' keydown cases at text-editor.ts:957-968. Repo-wide grep for toggleList shows the only test-side callers are EditorAPI.toggleList (list-heading-roundtrip.test.ts:209-244 -> editor.ts:2866, a separate implementation), a typeof/not.toThrow smoke check on the text-box implementation (text-box-editor.test.ts:327-334 -> text-box-editor.ts:1121), and vi.fn()/no-op stubs in frontend/slides tests. I enumerated every KeyboardEvent keydown dispatch under packages/docs/test/view (editor-tab-bullet.test.ts:89-95, backward-selection-toggle.test.ts:103, pending-style-editor.test.ts:117, header-table-nav.test.ts:76, editor-read-only.test.ts:184-223, text-box-editor.test.ts:762,900): keys used are Tab/Enter/Backspace/Delete/arrows/a/b/i/c/v/backslash — never a digit with shiftKey. Repo-wide searches for key:'7'/'8', Digit7/Digit8, Shift+7/Shift+8 and press('...7/8') hit only the documentation strings in src/view/shortcuts-catalog.ts:73-74; shortcuts-catalog.test.ts asserts catalog metadata only and invokes no handler. There is no e2e directory. TextEditor is constructed at editor.ts:2084 and text-box-editor.ts:668 but neither API toggleList delegates to it, so there is no indirect route. Hence the new heading-restoring exit at this call site has no test that can fail if it regresses to hardcoded 'paragraph'. (Mitigating but not refuting: the shared helper unlistedBlockType is unit-tested at list-heading-roundtrip.test.ts:129-139 and one of the three call sites is covered end-to-end.)

finding.summary: The new 'headingLevel is inert on a list-item' invariant is asserted in a comment but nothing tests it (export/serialize/clipboard readers)
finding.evidence: The change introduces a genuinely new document state — a `list-item` block that carries `headingLevel` — and the `Block` doc comment claims 'every reader (export, `blockStyleId`, toolbar labels) gates on `type === 'heading'`'. No test in the diff or the suite feeds such a block to any reader. I checked markdown serialization (src/serialize/markdown.ts:103), pdf outline (src/export/pdf-exporter.ts:201), docx export (src/export/docx-exporter.ts:184), `blockStyleId` (src/model/named-styles.ts:99) and clipboard copy (`cloneBlockWithFreshIds`, text-editor.ts:3404, which copies `headingLevel` verbatim, plus paste head/tail merges at text-editor.ts:3578/3607). The new tests assert only `type`/`headingLevel` fields on the store and Doc; if any of those readers stopped gating on type, or a copied bulleted heading pasted into body text resurrected as a heading, every test in this diff would still pass.
